ZK3O402wf1c.summary: The first lecture of Gilbert Strang's MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra course, covering the geometry of linear equations. It opens a full 35-lecture university course.
ZK3O402wf1c.why: It is HN's default recommendation for learning linear algebra, praised for Strang's teaching and for building real understanding useful in machine learning.

ZSRHeXYDLko.summary: A DevGAMM talk by Jonathan Blow arguing that civilizations can lose technological capability and that software quality is already deteriorating. He discusses how knowledge fails to transfer between generations.
ZSRHeXYDLko.why: It is the standard link in HN threads about software decay, lost knowledge and fragile technological civilization.

ZhuHCtR3xq8.summary: Microsoft's Brian Beckman gives an hour-long, whiteboard-style walk through monads, building from function composition and monoids using school-level math. It is aimed at practicing programmers rather than category theorists.
ZhuHCtR3xq8.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the clearest and most correct beginner explanation of monads, with several commenters saying it finally made them click.

ZuvK-od647c.summary: Veritasium explains quantum entanglement and spooky action at a distance, walking through Bell's inequality and the experiments that rule out hidden variables, in under ten minutes.
ZuvK-od647c.why: HN recommends it as one of the clearest layman explanations of Bell's theorem.

Z1PCtIaM_GQ.summary: Every Frame a Painting analyzes how Jackie Chan stages action comedy, with nine principles such as starting from a disadvantage, using the environment, clear shots, and keeping action and reaction in the same frame.
Z1PCtIaM_GQ.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the clearest explanation of why Chan's fight scenes beat fast-cut Hollywood action.

ZUvGfuLlZus.summary: Deviant Ollam's two-hour conference talk explains how elevators work, from the pit and buffers to the car top, controller logic and access-control features. It shows how this knowledge can be used for optimization and for bypassing building security.
ZUvGfuLlZus.why: HN commenters call it an absorbing, entertaining deep dive on elevator security and the go-to link whenever elevators come up.

ZmNOAtZIgIk.summary: Andrew Ng presents unsupervised feature learning and deep learning, showing how algorithms can learn representations from unlabeled data instead of hand-designed features. He gives examples in vision and audio, including visualizations of features learned by successive layers.
ZmNOAtZIgIk.why: HN commenters recommended it for years as a simple, exciting overview of the deep learning wave.

Z7Wl2FW2TcA.summary: Moxie Marlinspike's BlackHat 2011 talk examines weaknesses of SSL and the certificate authority system and proposes Convergence, a decentralized notary approach with trust agility.
Z7Wl2FW2TcA.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as the best explanation of why the CA system is broken and what alternatives exist.

Z4oYSByyRak.summary: Andrew Kelley, creator of Zig, introduces the language at the Recurse Center's Localhost series in 2018. He covers its goals of robustness, optimality and clarity, C interop, cross-compilation and explicit allocators.
Z4oYSByyRak.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the definitive introduction to Zig straight from its author, and links to it whenever Zig's design choices come up.

Zk11vI-7czE.summary: Planet of the Humans, a full documentary by Jeff Gibbs presented by Michael Moore, arguing that the green movement has been co-opted by corporate and wealthy interests and that techno-fixes are not enough.
Zk11vI-7czE.why: HN uses it as a contrarian critique of renewables and green tech, often recommended with caveats about bias and flawed conclusions.

ZDnShu5V99s.summary: A Google Tech Talk by Steve Weis that introduces modern cryptography and its use in practice and at Google. It covers proofs of security and security definitions and a special topic. HN commenters treat it as a talk on verifiable electronic voting.
ZDnShu5V99s.why: HN keeps pointing to it as a long, fascinating talk on cryptographic, verifiable voting whenever e-voting security comes up.

ZeecOKBus3Q.summary: Robert Miles explains instrumental convergence: why an AGI with almost any goal would tend to pursue sub-goals like self-preservation and resource acquisition. It builds on Omohundro's basic AI drives and his orthogonality thesis video.
ZeecOKBus3Q.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as the clearest introduction to why smart AI might behave badly by default.

ZTC_RxWN_xo.summary: Steve Blank's Computer History Museum lecture argues that Silicon Valley's roots lie in WWII radar and electronic warfare work, Stanford's Fred Terman and Cold War military funding rather than the semiconductor alone.
ZTC_RxWN_xo.why: HN commenters call it a favorite introduction to Valley history and cite it whenever government and military funding of tech comes up.

ZWQ0591PAxM.summary: Morphcat Games explains how they fit Micro Mages, a full-featured NES game, into 40 kilobytes. It covers compression of sprites and level layouts and other space-saving tricks.
ZWQ0591PAxM.why: HN points to it whenever discussion turns to how old games were so small, as a clear tour of 8-bit optimization and creative work under hardware limits.

ZXJWO2FQ16c.summary: A full performance of Steve Reich's Music for 18 Musicians by eighth blackbird with Third Coast Percussion and others, recorded in Chicago in 2011. It is an hour-long minimalist piece built on phasing and repeating patterns.
ZXJWO2FQ16c.why: Recommended in coding-music threads as lyric-free, repetitive music that aids focus.

Z1qyvQsjK5Y.summary: Casey Muratori's 2005 video introducing immediate-mode GUIs as an alternative to retained widget toolkits. He explains the motivation and shows minimal-state button logic.
Z1qyvQsjK5Y.why: Seen as the origin of the IMGUI idea that inspired Dear ImGui, recommended to anyone curious about immediate-mode UI design.

ZMByI4s-D-Y.summary: Veritasium explains the effort to redefine the kilogram, which was still defined by a physical artifact, and how a near-perfect silicon sphere from the Avogadro project helps. It also covers the history of the unit's odd naming.
ZMByI4s-D-Y.why: Recommended in kilogram-redefinition threads as a clear, short explainer of the Avogadro and Planck approaches.

Z2DU0qLfPIY.summary: Chris McCord's ElixirConf 2018 keynote introduces Phoenix LiveView, which renders HTML on the server and updates the page over websockets. It includes a demo showing that latency is not the bottleneck one might expect.
Z2DU0qLfPIY.why: HN recommends it as the original LiveView announcement and demo, a compelling argument for server-side rendering as an alternative to JavaScript front ends.

ZKC3hiyLeRc.summary: Dr. Jason Fung, a nephrologist, presents his view of the causes of obesity and type 2 diabetes, focusing on hormones such as insulin rather than calories alone. The talk draws on research and his Intensive Dietary Management program.
ZKC3hiyLeRc.why: HN commenters recommend it as a research-heavy introduction to how food type and hormones affect fat storage.

Ztc6QPNUqls.summary: Veritasium explains that the Higgs boson accounts for only a small fraction of everyday mass. Most of a proton's mass comes from the energy of the gluon field binding its quarks.
Ztc6QPNUqls.why: Recommended as a clear explanation of where mass actually comes from.

Z7rd04KzLcg.summary: Eric Weinstein's roughly three-hour presentation of Geometric Unity, his proposed theory unifying physics, given as a special episode of The Portal. It includes clarifications at the end.
Z7rd04KzLcg.why: HN uses it as the primary source for Weinstein's theory, though some commenters note he never published a full math paper.

ZCuYPiUIONs.summary: Lin Clark gives an illustrated, cartoon-style walkthrough of React Fiber, the rewrite of React's reconciler, explaining its incremental rendering and scheduling at React Conf 2017.
ZCuYPiUIONs.why: HN commenters recommend it as the clearest explanation of how Fiber and React 16 work.

ZDR433b0HJY.summary: Scott Chacon introduces Git by showing what happens under the hood for basic commands: staging, committing, data storage, branching, merging and pushing. He contrasts it with Subversion and shows history viewing with log.
ZDR433b0HJY.why: HN commenters keep recommending it as the best video for newcomers who want to understand how Git works technically.

ZD_3_gsgsnk.summary: Kirsten Dirksen visits retired mailman Russ Finch in Alliance, Nebraska, who grows oranges, figs and pomegranates in a backyard greenhouse without paying for heat. The greenhouse uses the stable temperature of the earth, with underground earth tubes, to heat and cool itself.
ZD_3_gsgsnk.why: HN commenters bring it up in geothermal, greenhouse and vertical farming threads as a low-tech example of growing citrus in a cold climate.

ZMQbHMgK2rw.summary: Veritasium visits the Micromouse competition, where small autonomous robots race to solve mazes at extreme speed. It covers the competition's technical history, including fans and ground effect enabling very high-g turns.
ZMQbHMgK2rw.why: HN commenters point to it as a nice introduction to micromouse and maze-racing robots.

ZPoqNeR3_UA.summary: A 24-hour loop of Star Trek TNG starship engine ambience, meant as background sound for relaxing, sleeping or concentrating.
ZPoqNeR3_UA.why: HN people use it as background noise for coding and focus, and share it as a personal favorite.

Z-9rLlFgcm0.summary: Michael Levin presents his lab's work on how cellular collectives use bioelectric networks to make anatomical decisions. Topics include pattern memories, regeneration and synthetic living organisms.
Z-9rLlFgcm0.why: HN commenters push it as an example of Levin's talks, which they think deserve far more attention.

ZEl-Y1NvBVI.summary: Primitive Technology shows building a cord drill from scratch and then upgrading it to a pump drill, using only primitive materials like a stone flywheel and cord.
ZEl-Y1NvBVI.why: HN people link it as a satisfying demonstration of hand-powered drills being made from nothing.

ZQFzMfHIxng.summary: Fedor Pikus's CppCon 2017 talk on C++ atomics, looking at what they let the programmer express and what the hardware actually does. It covers memory ordering and lock-free programming from basic to advanced.
ZQFzMfHIxng.why: HN recommends it as an enlightening explanation of atomics, caches and memory ordering from a strong presenter.

ZYj4NkeGPdM.summary: Owen Maitzen's animated hour-long introduction to Hackenbush, a simple combinatorial game, and how its strategy leads to surreal numbers and the roots of the number system.
ZYj4NkeGPdM.why: HN recommends it as an accessible, well-visualized entry point to Hackenbush, surreal numbers and their link to Nim.

ZecQ64l-gKM.summary: Lex Fridman interviews University of Glasgow chemist Lee Cronin about the origin of life, aliens, complexity and consciousness. The conversation centers on Cronin's assembly theory.
ZecQ64l-gKM.why: HN points to it in origin-of-life and complexity threads as a fascinating long-form introduction to assembly theory.

ZfuierUvx1A.summary: Chaos Theory is a 64k demoscene intro by Conspiracy and CNS that took second place at Assembly 2006, generating its graphics and music from a tiny executable.
ZfuierUvx1A.why: HN people use it as a showcase of what fits in 64 kilobytes.

ZggCipbiHwE.summary: A short supercut showing many Sinclair-owned local news anchors reading the same scripted warning about biased news, word for word.
ZggCipbiHwE.why: HN cites it as a vivid example of coordinated messaging and media consolidation, though some mentions use the title only as a quip.

ZsRRCnque2E.summary: Michael Steil's 25C3 talk covers the Commodore 64's architecture, quirks and demoscene tricks in about an hour. It aims to convey everything about the machine in a compact, nostalgic tour.
ZsRRCnque2E.why: HN people treat it as the canonical C64 talk and rewatch Steil's 'Ultimate' series regularly.

ZuXzvjBYW8A.summary: Lord David Willetts argues at the Royal Institution that the post-war baby boomers gained wealth and security at the expense of younger generations. He draws on his book The Pinch, covering housing, wealth and social policy in the UK.
ZuXzvjBYW8A.why: HN commenters point to it as a clear exposition of intergenerational unfairness in housing and wages, especially from a UK angle.

Z20XNp-luNA.summary: Karla Burnett presents real phishing campaigns run against a Bay Area tech company, including conversion rates and how existing protections were bypassed. She argues for evidence-based techniques to prevent credential phishing, not just mitigate it.
Z20XNp-luNA.why: HN people cite it to show even technical users fall for phishing and that hardware security keys are the real fix.

Z8ZhQPaw4rE.summary: Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 film Solaris, in which a psychologist is sent to a space station orbiting a planet with an alien intelligence and meets his dead wife there. It is the full movie, uploaded by Mosfilm.
Z8ZhQPaw4rE.why: HN recommends it as a masterpiece of emotional, contemplative science fiction, and draws analogies between its alien ocean and AI.

ZBtMbBPzqHY.summary: A 60 Minutes segment in which Navy pilots describe encounters with unidentified aerial phenomena, ahead of a report due to Congress.
ZBtMbBPzqHY.why: HN commenters point to it as eyewitness testimony and multi-radar evidence in UFO threads, though some dispute it.

ZC5Zr3NC2PY.summary: Technology Connections shows a cheap method for capturing analog video: a composite-to-HDMI upscaler feeding an HDMI capture dongle, aimed at digitizing home movies and VHS tapes.
ZC5Zr3NC2PY.why: HN people recommend it as an affordable, good-quality way to digitize analog video.

ZCmnQR3_qWg.summary: Daniel J. Bernstein and Tanja Lange survey recent highlights in post-quantum cryptography at 35C3, covering the NIST competition, network protocol experiments, and broken candidates.
ZCmnQR3_qWg.why: HN recommends it as a good overview of the NIST candidates and the state of post-quantum crypto.

ZLWMQLMiTPk.summary: Velcro's follow-up to its "Don't Say Velcro" ad responds to viewer feedback, with a humorous take on trademark usage and alternative names for hook and loop fasteners.
ZLWMQLMiTPk.why: HN recommends it as a delightful sequel to the original ad, brought up in threads on trademarks and the original campaign.

ZOzZ8R4gphE.summary: Andreas Kling ports the game Diablo to SerenityOS, his from-scratch Unix-like operating system, using the devilutionX project. The roughly 80-minute session shows what porting third-party software to the OS involves.
ZOzZ8R4gphE.why: HN commenters recommend it as a demonstration of SerenityOS's hackability and fast iteration across all layers of the system.

ZQc9-seU-5k.summary: Konrad Malawski's Strange Loop 2023 talk shows how the FoundationDB team adopted Swift incrementally in a C++ codebase. It covers Swift's C++ interoperability, which let them move single functions or entire types over one at a time.
ZQc9-seU-5k.why: HN commenters recommend it as the main resource on Swift as an incremental successor to C++ and on how the interoperability works in practice.

ZRV3pBuPxEQ.summary: Aaron Francis walks through how PHP has changed from 2012 to 2023, covering traits, array destructuring, generators, typed properties and more. It is a quick chaptered tour of modern PHP features.
ZRV3pBuPxEQ.why: HN commenters share it to show that modern PHP is much better than its reputation.

ZSPkcpGmflE.summary: An 8-minute National Geographic short film about David Bamberger, who bought 5,500 overgrazed acres in the Texas Hill Country and restored the land and its aquifers over about 50 years.
ZSPkcpGmflE.why: Cited in climate and water threads as an encouraging example of large-scale landscape restoration.

ZUG9qYTJMsI.summary: Dollar Shave Club's low-budget launch ad, in which the founder jokes his way through the case for cheap mail-order razors.
ZUG9qYTJMsI.why: HN holds it up as a great example of a funny, viral company video that frames the razor market well.

ZerUbHmuY04.summary: A silent PLOS ONE video of New Caledonian crows solving Aesop's Fable puzzles by dropping objects to raise water and reach food. It shows example trials from experiments testing causal understanding of water displacement.
ZerUbHmuY04.why: Used as vivid evidence of crow intelligence and animal physical reasoning in discussions of cognition.

Z0oFJ2jbkDI.summary: Kirsten Dirksen profiles Steve Rees, who buried two shipping containers to build an earth-cooled, off-grid 640 sq ft home in Northern California for about $30,000, solar included.
Z0oFJ2jbkDI.why: Recommended as an example of earth-sheltered housing and as part of a channel HN loves for architecture and efficiency.

Z2o_Sp2-aBo.summary: Applied Science builds a replica Apollo DSKY using an electroluminescent driver circuit and screen-printed conductive ink, with source and PCB files published.
Z2o_Sp2-aBo.why: HN people recommend it as a fantastic maker project among Apollo anniversary builds.

ZlfIVEy_YOA.summary: A short Stanford video in which Chao-Lin Kuo surprises Professor Andrei Linde with BICEP2 evidence supporting cosmic inflation, the first apparent images of primordial gravitational waves.
ZlfIVEy_YOA.why: Shared for its moving moment of scientific discovery, and later cited as a cautionary example after the BICEP2 result was retracted.

ZDxLa6P6exc.summary: LGR looks at the Silicon Graphics Indigo2, a UNIX workstation that cost about $86,000 in 1995, covering its pros and cons, games it can run, and whether it is worth owning today.
ZDxLa6P6exc.why: Recommended in threads about SGI and vintage workstations as a good look at the hardware.

ZTdUmlGxVo0.summary: A 27c3 talk on the Linux desktop (GNOME) by Wolfgang Draxinger, repeatedly interrupted and corrected by Lennart Poettering from the audience. The description notes much of the talk's content is disputed.
ZTdUmlGxVo0.why: HN points to it as a vivid example of the clash between two philosophies of Linux desktop design, often in systemd and Wayland arguments, though many find it disrespectful.

ZV-AFnCkRLY.summary: A timelapse of Notch (Markus Persson) making Metagun, a game built from scratch in 48 hours for Ludum Dare 18. It shows the whole coding session sped up.
ZV-AFnCkRLY.why: HN holds it up as a vivid example of focused game-jam productivity, and it has been used to demystify programming for students and inspire tools for recording coding sessions.

ZW5_eEKEC28.summary: Cuong Do of YouTube describes how a handful of engineers scaled the site, covering hardware, software and database scalability challenges during its rapid growth. The talk was given at the 2007 Seattle Conference on Scalability.
ZW5_eEKEC28.why: HN recommends it as a rich, concrete look at real-world system design and as evidence of YouTube's early Python stack.

ZXtimhT-ff4.summary: Ten hours of uninterrupted pink noise, intended for relaxation and masking background sound. It is a long ambient audio loop rather than a spoken video.
ZXtimhT-ff4.why: HN users use it as a concentration, sleep and tinnitus aid, preferring steady noise over music.

ZZs2HUW9tDA.summary: A short Coding Secrets episode explaining why hitting a Sonic 3D cartridge triggers a hidden level select. The cause was a custom crash handler that redirected CPU error interrupts to the level select screen.
ZZs2HUW9tDA.why: Shared as a favorite game-development anecdote with a clear technical explanation.

Zd_UcjMusUA.summary: Drummer Larnell Lewis hears Metallica's Enter Sandman for the first time on Drumeo and learns to play it by ear, using his musical vocabulary.
Zd_UcjMusUA.why: Cited as an inspiring example of quickly picking up a new piece by ear and of expertise transferring across genres.

Ze2pc6NwsHQ.summary: A Huberman Lab episode on setting up a workspace for productivity, focus and creativity, covering light, posture, movement and sound. It touches on ideas like ceiling height and the effect of screens on the brain.
Ze2pc6NwsHQ.why: Pointed to when people ask for science-based ways to boost concentration or arrange a home office.

Zklo4Z1SqkE.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder explains why hydrogen is a poor answer for decarbonization, covering how most hydrogen comes from fossil fuels, the efficiency losses of green hydrogen and reliance on rare metals in fuel cells.
Zklo4Z1SqkE.why: HN cites it in hydrogen strategy threads as a concise skeptical summary of why hydrogen is not yet viable.

ZmWREtcDVBE.summary: Tom Scott races a London black-cab driver who has memorized The Knowledge against a phone GPS across the city, comparing local expertise to navigation software.
ZmWREtcDVBE.why: HN people link it in discussions of taxi drivers' spatial memory and how cabbies handle roadworks and traffic.

Zn7oWIhFffs.summary: Chris Stucchio presents the ethical principles behind algorithmic decision making and shows with examples from lending, criminology and education that they cannot all be satisfied at once. The talk frames AI fairness as a set of quantitative tradeoffs.
Zn7oWIhFffs.why: HN cites it in algorithmic-bias threads for the impossibility result that an algorithm cannot be procedurally fair, group fair and maximally useful at once.

ZHqFrNyLlpA.summary: A live-coded demo by Jonathan Blow showing how to get object-system-style expressiveness in a data-oriented way, covering structure-of-arrays layouts and composition. It shows features of his Jai language that make programs fast.
ZHqFrNyLlpA.why: HN points to it as the practical demonstration of data-oriented design, including structure packing and switching between AOS and SOA.

Zpnncakrelk.summary: Bryan Cantrill's OSCON 2015 talk on moving a proprietary product to open source, drawing on Sun's history with Solaris and illumos, licensing choices and the relicensing after Oracle's acquisition.
Zpnncakrelk.why: HN commenters cite it for the history of open source at Sun and Oracle, and for Cantrill's explanation of licensing choices.

ZxYOEwM6Wbk.summary: A 3Blue1Brown live lockdown math episode asking what Euler's formula e^(pi i) is actually saying. It builds intuition through exponentials, rotation and vectors landing on the unit circle.
ZxYOEwM6Wbk.why: HN recommends it as the explanation that makes complex exponentials click, especially for understanding the Fourier transform.

Z0DAKaR16cY.summary: Brady Haran interviews Brother Guy Consolmagno, director of the Vatican Observatory, for Sixty Symbols. It is part of a three-video set along with the observatory's telescopes and its meteorite collection.
Z0DAKaR16cY.why: HN links it as an approachable interview with a working astronomer who is also a Jesuit, whenever the Vatican Observatory or science and religion comes up.

Z2ZXW2HBLPM.summary: Paul Irish explains how pointerpointer.com works. It uses a hidden canvas of colored Voronoi regions to look up which photo matches the cursor position.
Z2ZXW2HBLPM.why: HN links it as the author's own breakdown of Pointer Pointer's inner workings.

ZH2wGpEZVgE.summary: A Design Club episode that analyzes how Super Mario Bros. level 1-1 teaches players to play through level design alone, without text tutorials.
ZH2wGpEZVgE.why: HN cites it as the standard walkthrough of Mario's implicit teaching and as an example of hiding the tutorial inside the problem.

ZI198eFghJk.summary: Chandler Carruth's CppNow 2023 talk on modernizing compiler design for the Carbon toolchain, using data-oriented design and modern hardware assumptions. It covers lexing, parsing and compact data structures aimed at compiler performance.
ZI198eFghJk.why: Recommended as a recent take on rethinking compiler architecture, and cited in discussions of flattened ASTs and fast lexers.

ZJUyVVFOXOc.summary: Steve Yegge shows Efrit, a tool that gives Claude full control of Emacs, on the Vibe Coding with Steve and Gene show. Claude opens info pages, runs shells and even draws a Mandelbrot fractal in a buffer.
ZJUyVVFOXOc.why: HN shares it as a fun demo of an LLM driving a live Emacs process and orchestrating its long-standing ecosystem.

ZN4njIQcSR4.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment examines prediction markets such as Polymarket: the legal and moral questions, weak regulation, and insider trading and manipulation concerns.
ZN4njIQcSR4.why: HN cites it in prediction-market threads as an accessible critical overview, including the Polymarket CEO's remarks on insider trading.

ZPbyDSvGasw.summary: A DEFCON 21 talk by Robert Stucke on DNS errors caused by single-bit flips, which lead to requests for misspelled domains. It shows real-world data on bitsquatting.
ZPbyDSvGasw.why: Cited in threads on ECC memory, CPU reliability, and bitsquatting as evidence that bit flips cause real DNS misdirection.

ZR0ujwlvbkQ.summary: A lecture by Commodore Grace Hopper on the future of computing, posted by MIT Lincoln Laboratory. It includes her well-known nanosecond wire demonstration and humorous comparisons of device latencies.
ZR0ujwlvbkQ.why: Cited for her vivid illustration of orders of magnitude in latency, and as an example of a great computing pioneer as teacher.

ZRkm6-bBk4U.summary: Sandy Munro sits down with engineers from 3IS to compare the electrical architectures of the Tesla Model Y, Ford Mach-E and VW ID.4. They discuss ECU counts, bus architectures and what the differences mean for cost and integration.
ZRkm6-bBk4U.why: HN recommends it as a fair, technical comparison and cites it when discussing why legacy automakers have more boxes and complexity than Tesla.

ZTidn2dBYbY.summary: The official music video for David Hasselhoff's synthwave track True Survivor, written for the film Kung Fury. It is an 80s-style pop song from the Kickstarter-funded movie.
ZTidn2dBYbY.why: Mostly mentioned as a joke or a personal pick, including on a coding playlist thread.

ZW8gWgpptI8.summary: Adam Robinson-Yu's GDC 2020 talk on how he shelved a big project to prototype what became A Short Hike. He covers the solo development process and technical choices like a pixel shader over low-poly models.
ZW8gWgpptI8.why: HN people cite it for solo-dev inspiration and for the rendering technique behind the game's look.

ZYD9yyMh9Hk.summary: A PyData London 2018 talk on how JPMorgan scaled its Athena Python platform over ten years to about 35 million lines of code and thousands of developers. It covers infrastructure, tooling and culture for analytics and visualization at that scale.
ZYD9yyMh9Hk.why: Cited as the definitive public account of Python at massive scale, especially in discussions of monorepos and bank Python.

ZYqG31V4qtA.summary: Linus Tech Tips reviews AMD's Ryzen 9 4900HS mobile CPU in the ASUS ROG Zephyrus G14 laptop, calling it a landmark product. It highlights strong performance against Intel along with good efficiency and battery life.
ZYqG31V4qtA.why: HN people cite it as a review showing Zen 2's efficiency and performance advantage over Intel in laptops.

ZZ3F3zWiEmc.summary: A Wendover Productions video on how the art market works, arguing that prices are driven by wealth, storage and tax mechanics rather than artistic value.
ZZ3F3zWiEmc.why: Used to explain why contemporary art is expensive for money reasons rather than art reasons.

Za45bT41sXg.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on food safety in the US. It looks at the FDA, the USDA and industry groups such as the Association for Dressings and Sauces, and how little enforcement there is.
Za45bT41sXg.why: HN cites it as an overview of overlapping and underfunded food regulation.

ZvmMzI0X7fE.summary: D. Richard Hipp's PGCon 2014 keynote on SQLite's relationship to PostgreSQL. He explains that SQLite was originally written from PostgreSQL 6.5 documentation and that the two engines serve different classes of problems.
ZvmMzI0X7fE.why: Recommended as a talk from SQLite's main author, and cited for the project's focus on backwards compatibility and for deployment anecdotes.

ZzsK8Am6dKU.summary: A Stanford talk by Matthew Might on parsing with derivatives, a new way to write parsers, and why better parsing tools are needed. It discusses language theory and criticizes ad-hoc hand-written parsers.
ZzsK8Am6dKU.why: Mentioned as a great talk and related reading in threads on parsing techniques.

Z1EA2ohrt5Q.summary: A 1984 interview with former KGB agent Yuri Bezmenov on ideological subversion and psychological warfare, reposted in 2020 with a modern political framing.
Z1EA2ohrt5Q.why: HN commenters cite it as a source on Soviet subversion tactics and propaganda, usually in political threads.

Z3dSkkEr-wk.summary: A short comedic complaint by ProZD about YouTube search failing to surface his own video even when searching its exact title. It illustrates how poor search results have become.
Z3dSkkEr-wk.why: Cited as a concrete example of YouTube and Google search failing to find content by exact title.

ZBEqyiO35cQ.summary: A CNBC interview in which Deirdre Bosa talks with Tether's CTO and general counsel about the company's role in crypto and the future of stablecoins.
ZBEqyiO35cQ.why: HN cites it critically, as an example of Tether executives dodging questions about reserves and backing.

ZDOI0cq6GZM.summary: The Monorail song scene from The Simpsons, uploaded with a note comparing it to a local Australian development controversy.
ZDOI0cq6GZM.why: HN uses it as a recurring joke whenever hyperloop or grand transit schemes come up.

ZITP93pqtdQ.summary: A short clip of Gary Johnson being booed at a Libertarian Party debate for saying he supports driver's licenses.
ZITP93pqtdQ.why: Used as a punchline or example to mock hardline libertarian positions, not as a recommendation.

ZJL_8kNFmTI.summary: A local news report about a woman who ordered a pizza on a 911 call to discreetly signal domestic violence and give her address to the dispatcher. The coverage includes the actual dispatcher call.
ZJL_8kNFmTI.why: Cited as a real example of coded language used to get help in emergency calls without alerting an abuser.

ZMGCFLEYakM.summary: Short footage of the General Electric Cybernetic Anthropomorphous Machine, or Walking Truck, a 1960s quadruped vehicle operated by a human driver using hydraulic limbs. The uploader notes it predates Big Dog by decades.
ZMGCFLEYakM.why: HN cites it in robotics threads as proof that legged machines were mechanically feasible in the 1960s, long before Boston Dynamics.

ZNVuIU6UUiM.summary: Tom Scott visits the British Library, a UK legal deposit library that receives a copy of everything published, and discusses storing so much material, including the web archive.
ZNVuIU6UUiM.why: HN commenters cite it to explain why legal deposit should be complete rather than selective.

ZO0PXYMVGSU.summary: A two-hour Computer History Museum oral history interview with Bjarne Stroustrup, conducted by Paul McJones in 2015. It covers his youth, education at Aarhus and Cambridge, his career at Bell Labs and elsewhere, and the design and evolution of C++.
ZO0PXYMVGSU.why: HN commenters cite it as a primary source for why Stroustrup created C++, including combining C and Simula and the aim of zero-cost abstractions.

ZORzsubQA_M.summary: A short Vox video on Barcelona's superblocks, an urban design approach that closes interior streets to through traffic to return space to pedestrians.
